A.note: Best frame by a clear margin. It has ships at anchor, a rock, smoke, campfires and troop formations in ranks, under natural light with believable grass. The troops are small and a bit uniform, like game units, and the ground is slightly flat. It still reads as a siege camp.

B.note: The ground is an almost empty ochre field with faint pale scuffs where the camps should be. The rock and sea are fine, but there are no troops, smoke or lines. Nothing says siege. The texture is natural, but the frame is monotonous.

C.note: The camps are tiled rectangles with dot-sized figures, so they read as a map overlay or a texture. The terrain is flat green and yellow colour fields. Scale is unclear and the rock is tiny. It is washed out and has no atmosphere.

D.note: Similar to C but flatter and emptier. It has a uniform yellow-green plane, faint grid-like camp patches and almost no distinct detail. It looks like a plain diagram and has no ships, smoke or readable troops.

why: A is the only frame that shows a believable siege, with ships, smoke, fires and troop formations in a lit landscape. B, C and D are mostly empty or flat terrain where the camps are unreadable.
top_fix_for_best: Add scale and depth to A. Use larger, closer foreground troops, tents, earthworks and cannon batteries, and darker, denser smoke columns. Vary the troop poses and uniform colours so the ranks stop reading as repeated game pieces, and put real texture and shadow on the ground. Add a visible fortified rock with walls, so the siege target reads.
